# Lite requirements document — Text preview

Text preview lets someone see the opening lines of a text file without opening it in an
editor. It matters because finding the right file today means opening files one by one,
and every opening risks changing a file by accident.

**Date:** 2026-09-13
**Author:** Generated by the shape skill from the intake interview
**Profile:** software (of config: software)
**Entry point:** interview
**Status:** approved (2026-09-13)
**Decomposition:** populated (2026-09-13)
**Notes:** UX ideation skipped: not UI-facing (the project configuration records this work as having no user-interface screens)

---

## 1. Problem & Context

**What problem does this solve?**
There is no way to see what a text file contains without opening it in an editor. Finding
the right file means opening candidates one by one, and opening a file only to look at it
risks changing it by accident. Text preview shows a file's opening lines with no editor and
no chance of changing the file.

**Goals:**
- A file's opening lines are visible without opening an editor.
- The preview cannot change the file.
- The preview shows the file as it is at the moment it is requested.

**Who is affected?**
- People browsing files, typically data analysts: they open each candidate file in an
  editor to check its contents, which is slow and exposes the file to accidental edits.
- The maintainer: signs off on this feature. No other teams are affected.

**What exists today?**
Nothing previews a file. The only way to see its contents is to open it in an editor, one
file at a time, with the file open for changes.

---

## 2. Scope

**In Scope:**
- Show the first lines of a single text file.
- Read-only behaviour: previewing never changes the file.
- Show the file's contents as they are when the preview is requested.
- A plain note, instead of a preview, when the file is empty or is not text.

**Out of Scope:**
- Editing files.
- Previewing more than one file at once.
- Previewing non-text files (they receive the plain note, never a preview).

---

## 3. Units of Work

> Each unit is a capability a person can use on its own, and each becomes one Linear
> issue. Priority uses Linear's scale: **Urgent** / **High** / **Medium** / **Low**.

- **Unit 1 (Urgent):** Preview the opening lines of a text file. A person browsing files
  sees the first lines of one text file, current and read-only, without opening an editor.
- **Unit 2 (Urgent):** Say plainly when a file is empty or is not text. Instead of a blank
  or unreadable preview, the person sees a short note that the file is empty or is not a
  text file, so they can move on without opening it.

**Happy path:** Choose a text file → ask for a preview → read its first lines → Done.

---

## 4. Requirements

Each requirement has an identifier of the form FR-nnn, where FR stands for functional
requirement.

| ID | Description | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------------|----------|---------------------|
| FR-001 | Show the opening lines of one chosen text file without opening it in an editor | Urgent | For a text file longer than the preview length, exactly the first lines up to that length are shown, in file order. For a shorter text file, every line is shown. |
| FR-002 | Previewing never changes the file | Urgent | After a preview, the file's contents, size and last-modified time are unchanged. The preview offers no way to edit or save the file. |
| FR-003 | The preview reflects the file at the moment it is requested | Urgent | When a file changes between two previews, the second preview shows the changed lines; an earlier preview is never reused. |
| FR-004 | A plain note replaces the preview when the file is empty | Urgent | For a file with no content, the person sees a note saying the file is empty, and no preview lines. |
| FR-005 | A plain note replaces the preview when the file is not text | Urgent | For a file that is not text, such as an image, the person sees a note saying the file is not a text file and cannot be previewed, and none of the file's content is shown. |

Units map to requirements as follows: Unit 1 covers FR-001, FR-002 and FR-003; Unit 2
covers FR-004 and FR-005.

**Design-system components:** not applicable — this work has no user-interface screens.

**Key constraints:**
- Integrity: the preview reads files only; it never opens a file for writing.

---

## Open Questions

- [ ] How many opening lines does a preview show? Owner: the maintainer, before build.
- [ ] How is a file judged to be text or not text (for example, by its content or by its
  file extension)? Owner: the maintainer, before build.
- [ ] How does a person ask for a preview, and where is it shown? Owner: the maintainer,
  before build.
- [ ] What does the person see when a file cannot be read, such as a missing file or one
  they lack permission to open? This was not raised at intake. Owner: the maintainer,
  before build.

The maintainer owns all four open decisions and must settle them before build starts.
